passages.provision_quote: Athletic teams or sports designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex.
passages.note: Enacted text (Sec. 15-120.02.B) bars male-sex students from girls' teams while Sec. 15-120.02.C expressly preserves eligibility for boys'/coed teams, excluding a total ban.
House Third Reading roll call on single-subject SB 1165; Bolick voted Y, 31-24-5-0-0 (40% No, not near-unanimous).
Bill history page lists Bolick as a co-sponsor of SB 1165, which the governor signed into Chapter 106.

rows.reasoning: Bolick co-sponsored SB 1165 (2022) and voted Y on its House Third Reading (31-24-5-0-0); the enacted law provides that teams "designated for 'females', 'women' or 'girls' may not be open to students of the male sex" while expressly preserving participation on boys'/coed teams, matching rung 4 ("require transgender athletes to compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth") and excluding rung 5's complete ban. The act dates from her prior House term (2019-2023), the earlier chamber of the same legislature she now serves in as Senator, so it counts as in-term (V5 ruling 2026-09-27).
